definitions.definition: A software bundle of related state and behavior, often used to model things found in everyday life.
Blueprint or prototype from which objects are created.
Block declared like a method but with the name of the class and no return type, invoked to create objects from the class blueprint.
No-argument constructor that the compiler supplies for any class declaring none, which calls the no-argument constructor of the superclass.
Giving methods in one class the same name but different parameter lists, distinguished by the number and type of arguments.
Combination of a method's name and its parameter types, by which Java distinguishes methods.
Sequence of characters that Java represents as an object which cannot be changed once it is created.
Series of characters in code enclosed in double quotes, for which the compiler creates a String object with that value.
Keyword that determines whether other classes can use a particular field or invoke a particular method.
Modifier that restricts a member so it can be accessed only within its own class.
Modifier allowing a member to be accessed within its own package and also by subclasses of its class in other packages.
Default access level, with no modifier, under which a class is visible only within its own package.
Class derived from another class, also called a derived, extended or child class.
Class from which a subclass is derived, also called a base class or parent class.
Defining in a subclass an instance method with the same signature and return type as one in the superclass.
Defining in a subclass a static method with the same signature as a static method of the superclass.
Principle that subclasses can define their own unique behaviors while sharing some of the functionality of the parent class.
Behavior in which the JVM calls the method of the object a variable refers to, not the method defined by the variable's type.
Class declared abstract that may or may not include abstract methods; it cannot be instantiated but can be subclassed.
Method declared without an implementation, with no braces and followed by a semicolon.
A contract between a class and the outside world, whose published behavior any implementing class promises to provide.
Unlike an abstract class, it has only public static final fields, and a class can implement any number of them but extend only one class.
Grouping of related types that provides access protection and namespace management.
Sequence of data that represents an input source or an output destination.
Stream that a program uses to read data from a source, one item at a time.
Stream that a program uses to write data to a destination, one item at a time.
Object, sometimes called a container, that groups multiple elements into a single unit.
Unified architecture that represents and manipulates groups of elements through interfaces, implementations and algorithms.
Abstract data types that represent collections and let them be manipulated independently of the details of their representation.
Concrete implementations of the collection interfaces; in essence, reusable data structures.
Polymorphic methods that perform useful computations such as searching and sorting on objects implementing collection interfaces.
Event occurring during program execution that disrupts the normal flow of the program's instructions.
Creating an exception object and handing it to the runtime system.
Ordered list of methods that were called to reach the method where the error occurred.
Block of code in a method that the runtime system finds by searching the call stack and that can handle the error.
Choosing an exception handler to deal with a thrown error.
Block that always executes when the try block exits, so cleanup code is not accidentally bypassed by a return, continue or break.
Unit of execution with a self-contained execution environment, including its own private memory space.
Lightweight unit of execution within a process that shares the process's resources, including memory and open files.
Operating system feature by which processing time on a single core is shared among processes and threads.
Error introduced when multiple threads access shared data.
Error that results from threads having inconsistent views of shared memory.
Tool needed to prevent thread interference and memory consistency errors among threads sharing fields and objects.
Situation in which two or more threads try to access the same resource simultaneously, slowing or suspending some of them.
Tree of components that has a top-level container as its root, which every GUI component must belong to in order to appear.

definitions.definition: Root of a containment hierarchy; Swing provides three, named JFrame, JDialog and JApplet.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Part of a top-level container that contains, directly or indirectly, the visible components of its GUI.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Object implementing the LayoutManager interface that determines the size and position of components within a container.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Layout manager suited to displaying a few components of the same size in rows and columns.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Object that gives information about an occurrence and identifies the source that produced it.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Component, model or other object that produces an event.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Object implementing a listener interface such as ActionListener that registers with a component to be notified when its events fire.
definitions.unitTitle: GUI Programming, Swings and Event Handling

definitions.definition: Special kind of Java program that a Java-enabled browser downloads from the internet and runs, typically embedded in a web page.
Swing subclass of the Applet class, to be used for all applets that build their user interface from Swing components.
Connection-based protocol that provides a reliable flow of data between two computers, delivering it in the order sent.
Protocol that sends independent packets called datagrams with no guarantee of arrival or order, and without a connection.
16-bit number from 0 to 65535 that TCP and UDP use to deliver data to the right application.
Port numbers 0 to 1023, reserved for services such as HTTP and FTP, which applications should not bind to.
One endpoint of a two-way communication link between two programs on the network, bound to a port number.
Combination of an IP address and a port number, by which every TCP connection is uniquely identified.
